entries.title: Acts 28:1
segments: Melita. Malts.  The scene of Paul's shipwreck is, according to tradition, St. Paul's Bay, about eight miles northwest of Valetta, the capital of the island.

entries.title: Acts 28:2
segments: Barbarians. Those who were not Greeks and Romans were called barbarians.

entries.title: Acts 28:4
segments: Justice. The goddess of justice, according to the idolatrous notions of the natives.

entries.title: Acts 28:6
segments: Said that he was a god. As they did at Lystra.  See

entries.title: Acts 28:7
segments: The chief man. An inscription since discovered verifies this title.

entries.title: Acts 28:11
segments:
Whose sign, etc.  Meaning the figurehead.
 

 
Twin Brothers. Castor and Pollux.  In Roman mythology they were sons of Jupiter.  They were the favoring gods of sailors.

entries.title: Acts 28:12
segments: Syracuse. Capital city of the island of Sicily.  It was at this time a Roman colony, and was a hundred miles north of Malta.  For explanation of a Roman colony see note on

entries.title: Acts 28:13
segments:
Rhegium. A city at the southern extremity of Italy, on the Straits of Messina.  Its modern name is Reggio.
 

 
Puteoli. Then the chief port of Rome.  It was on the north shore of the Bay of Naples.

entries.title: Acts 28:15
segments:
The Market of Appius. A town on the Appian Way, and forty-three miles from Rome.  It was a great resort for sailors.
 

 
The Three Taverns. A place about ten miles nearer Rome than the Market of Appius.
